---
title: "Tips - Solutions"
output: html_document
---

### Introduction:

This exercise was created based on the tutorial and documentation from [Seaborn](https://stanford.edu/~mwaskom/software/seaborn/index.html)
The dataset being used is tips from Seaborn. Here every plot is made with ggplot2.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries:

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# set the ggplot2 style to white, without the right and upper borders
theme_set(theme_classic())
```

### Step 2. Import the dataset from this [address](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/07_Visualization/Tips/tips.csv).

### Step 3. Assign it to a variable called tips

```{r}
# the same file is also included in this folder: read_csv("tips.csv")
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/guipsamora/pandas_exercises/master/07_Visualization/Tips/tips.csv"
tips <- read_csv(url)

head(tips)
```

### Step 4. Delete the first (unnamed) column

```{r}
# the first column has no name in the file, so readr calls it "...1"
tips <- tips |> select(-1)

head(tips)
```

### Step 5. Plot the total_bill column histogram

```{r}
# histogram with a density curve on top (like seaborn's distplot)
ggplot(tips, aes(x = total_bill)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 20, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_density() +
  # set labels and titles
  labs(x = "Value", y = "Frequency", title = "Total Bill")
```

### Step 6. Create a scatter plot presenting the relationship between total_bill and tip

```{r}
ggplot(tips, aes(x = total_bill, y = tip)) +
  geom_point()
```

### Step 7. Create one image with the relationship of total_bill, tip and size.

#### Hint: It is just one function.

```{r}
# pairs() draws a scatterplot for every pair of columns.
# (GGally::ggpairs() is a ggplot2 alternative if you have GGally installed)
pairs(tips[c("total_bill", "tip", "size")])
```

### Step 8. Present the relationship between days and total_bill value

```{r}
ggplot(tips, aes(x = day, y = total_bill)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.1)
```

### Step 9. Create a scatter plot with the day as the y-axis and tip as the x-axis, differ the dots by sex

```{r}
ggplot(tips, aes(x = tip, y = day, color = sex)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.1)
```

### Step 10. Create a box plot presenting the total_bill per day differentiating the time (Dinner or Lunch)

```{r}
ggplot(tips, aes(x = day, y = total_bill, fill = time)) +
  geom_boxplot()
```

### Step 11. Create two histograms of the tip value based for Dinner and Lunch. They must be side by side.

```{r}
# facet_wrap() creates one panel per value of time
ggplot(tips, aes(x = tip)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 10) +
  facet_wrap(~ time)
```

### Step 12. Create two scatterplots graphs, one for Male and another for Female, presenting the total_bill value and tip relationship, differing by smoker or no smoker

### They must be side by side.

```{r}
ggplot(tips, aes(x = total_bill, y = tip, color = smoker)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ sex)
```
